# Benchmarks

**Generated by `npm run benchmark`. Do not edit by hand.**

Every figure here is produced by running the tool on a corpus generated from source, so it is reproducible on any
machine and reviewable in a diff. The corpus is in [`scripts/benchmark.mjs`](scripts/benchmark.mjs).

## Fidelity is the measurement that matters

**A 100% saving that drops the one failing test is a bug, not a win** — and a benchmark reporting only ratios cannot
tell those apart. So every corpus entry declares **needles**: the failing assertion, the error line, the value someone
would actually grep for. A row passes only if every needle is still **literally present** in the output.

Not "reconstructible" — present. An error you can only see after running a decoder is not visible to the reader the
output is for.

Budget: 4,000 characters. Node v22.15.0 on win32.

| Corpus | Before | After | Saved | Removed anything? | Needles kept | Transforms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Test suite, one failure | 16,125 | 3,935 | 75.6% | yes | 3/3 | log-templates, template-rows |
| Build log, six formats | 68,804 | 3,946 | 94.3% | yes | 2/2 | log-templates, template-rows |
| JSON API response, 300 records | 50,676 | 16,249 | 67.9% | **no** | 2/2 | json-tables |
| Stack trace, 300 frames | 13,809 | 3,994 | 71.1% | yes | 2/2 | stacktrace |
| Unified diff, 500 lines | 7,472 | 3,166 | 57.6% | **no** | 2/2 | log-templates |
| Scraped HTML article | 15,080 | 2,063 | 86.3% | yes | 2/2 | html-to-markdown |
| Plain prose (gistline does badly) | 29,891 | 3,995 | 86.6% | yes | 2/2 | log |
| CSV export, 400 rows | 18,329 | 3,995 | 78.2% | yes | 5/5 | log |

**8 of 8 corpora kept every needle.**

## Reading this honestly

**Best case:** Build log, six formats at 94.3%.

**Worst case:** Unified diff, 500 lines at 57.6%. That row is kept deliberately — prose has no repeated
structure to state once, so there is nothing to compact losslessly and the fallback is blunt. A benchmark showing only
wins is marketing.

**2 of 8 corpora were compressed with nothing removed at all**, which is the column worth
reading first. A lossless result means every value is still there, stated differently.

Where something *was* removed, the original remains retrievable by id — so the saving is safe rather than final.

## Timing

| Corpus | Time |
|---|---|
| Test suite, one failure | 36.5ms |
| Build log, six formats | 54.6ms |
| JSON API response, 300 records | 20.4ms |
| Stack trace, 300 frames | 3.9ms |
| Unified diff, 500 lines | 8.7ms |
| Scraped HTML article | 7.4ms |
| Plain prose (gistline does badly) | 1.1ms |
| CSV export, 400 rows | 27.2ms |

Deterministic and dependency-free: no model to load, no warm-up, and the same input produces byte-identical output on
every run. That is what makes it usable in a pre-commit hook.

## What is not measured here

- **Token counts.** Characters are a proxy. A real tokeniser would be exact and would be a dependency.
- **Comparison against other tools.** Their corpora and budgets differ, and a table built to flatter one tool is worth
  nothing. Run `npm run benchmark` on your own content instead.
- **Very large inputs.** Everything is read into memory; streaming is on the roadmap.

*Regenerate with `npm run benchmark`.*
